title: Expanding our paradigm for behavioral health: Psychology's role in advancing a population health approach.
abstract: Despite advances in evidence-based treatments, approximately half of individuals with diagnosable behavioral health conditions receive professional care. This treatment gap reflects a fundamental conceptual problem: defining behavioral health by services delivered rather than outcomes achieved. A population health paradigm offers a critical reframe of the "who, what, when, where, and how" of behavioral health-shifting from reactive crisis intervention to proactive, continuous support across the entire spectrum of need. This requires expanding who provides support beyond licensed clinicians, broadening goals from treating pathology to promoting wellness for all, intervening earlier in disease trajectories, embedding support in community settings, and employing diverse strategies grounded in research and community wisdom. Psychology's biopsychosocial perspective and scientist-practitioner model position the field to advance this approach, and health psychology serves as a critical bridge, connecting population health principles to practice and policy.
